source: datagrip-pgadmin lens census — jetbrains.com/datagrip feature pages (executing.html, data_editor.html, refactoring.html, editor.html), JetBrains blog "Top 9 SQL Features" + "Top 9 Spreadsheet Features" + DataGrip 2026.1 release notes, pgadmin.org docs (query_tool, schema_diff, erd_tool, dashboards, developer_tools), cross-checked against qwry docs/ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/ROADMAP_v0.5.md

findings.title: Run-statement-under-caret with visible statement boundary (DataGrip execution options)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip's ⌘Enter runs the statement under the caret, with a configurable ambiguity policy (smallest statement / largest / prompt via Statements chooser / whole script) and highlights the range it executed. WHY LOVED: it's the single most-used interaction in an SQL IDE — you work in one long scratch file and fire individual statements without selecting text. qwry has `statementRange()` in the splitter already and run-at-caret parked at v0.5 P2; this deserves promotion to P0. BEYOND: make the boundary permanent, not modal — a subtle always-on gutter bar marking the statement containing the caret (recomputed <16ms from the existing lexer), ⌘Enter runs exactly that range and flashes it, ⌘⇧Enter runs the whole buffer, ⌥⌘Enter runs selection-as-is. No prompt dialog ever (DataGrip's chooser popup is the slow part to beat). FITS CHARTER: perfectly — keyboard-first, zero-latency, builds on existing splitter.

findings.title: Schema-aware lint: unresolved table/column squiggles + did-you-mean (DataGrip inspections)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip underlines identifiers that don't resolve against the connected schema (unknown column, wrong alias scope, ambiguous column) before you run anything, with quick-fix suggestions. WHY LOVED: it converts the run→error→fix loop into a type-as-you-go loop; it's the thing that makes DataGrip feel like an IDE instead of a textarea. qwry already has lint.ts + the lezer-tree query-context walker + in-memory SchemaSnapshot — all ingredients exist, only the resolution pass is missing. BEYOND: fully synchronous zero-IPC resolution (DataGrip's is async and laggy on big schemas), squiggle with 'did you mean orders.created_at?' quick-fix applied by one keystroke, and alias-scope awareness reusing the completion engine's FROM/JOIN context. Also lint SELECT-list columns against GROUP BY. FITS CHARTER: core — this is the intellisense differentiator extended to diagnostics.

findings.title: Selection aggregates in the status bar (DataGrip Aggregate View)
findings.detail: WHAT: select any rectangle of cells in DataGrip and the Aggregate view shows SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX/COUNT/COUNT DISTINCT/NULL-count live; Excel users expect this reflexively. WHY LOVED: answers 'what do these 40 numbers add up to' without writing a query — the highest value-per-line-of-code grid feature that exists. qwry's selection model (selection.ts) already tracks rects. BEYOND: always-on, not a separate view — status bar shows `n=120 · sum 4,502.10 · avg 37.5 · null 3` the instant selection changes (computed over in-memory rows, trivially <16ms for 50k cap), click or shortcut cycles which metrics show, ⌘C on the readout copies it. Type-aware: numerics get sum/avg, text gets distinct-count, timestamps get min→max span. FITS CHARTER: perfectly — grid-is-the-app, pure client-side, zero server cost.

findings.title: Single-record / transpose view (DataGrip ⌘⇧Enter record view + View-as-Transpose)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip shows one row vertically (column name → value) in a side panel, editable, with arrows moving to next/prev record while staying transposed; separately a full-grid Transpose mode for wide tables. WHY LOVED: on a 60-column table the grid is unreadable; the record view is how people actually inspect a row. qwry's inspector is cell-scoped today; the roadmap's 'row → See details (inspector)' is the hook. BEYOND: promote the inspector to a row mode — Space or ⌘⇧Enter on a row shows all columns vertically with the same NULL-chip/type-icon rendering as the grid, dirty cells editable in place (reusing editsStore), ↑↓ walks rows while the panel stays open, ⌘F filters columns by name. Skip full-grid transpose (fights the two-axis virtualizer); the record panel covers 95% of the need. FITS CHARTER: yes — reuses the existing inspector card and per-tab state.

findings.title: Local history with diff and restore (DataGrip Local History)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip snapshots every editor change and lets you review/diff/restore any prior state of a console file, independent of VCS; saved developers from lost queries countless times. WHY LOVED: it's the ultimate expression of 'never lose work' — qwry's ideology #4 verbatim — and qwry already persists tab text to appdb but keeps only the latest state, so an accidental select-all-delete-type is unrecoverable. BEYOND: snapshot per-tab into rusqlite on every run + on 30s-idle-after-change (content-hashed, deduped, capped ~100/tab), a ⌘⇧H timeline overlay listing snapshots with timestamp + first line, arrow-key preview diffed inline against the current buffer (CodeMirror merge view), Enter restores. Effectively zero storage cost for SQL-sized text. FITS CHARTER: core — directly extends the never-lose-work invariant past what any competitor does for scratch SQL.

findings.title: Transaction-state awareness: in-txn chip + failed-transaction handling (DataGrip manual tx mode)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip exposes auto vs manual commit per data source, shows uncommitted state, and warns on close with an open transaction. WHY LOVED: the #1 way GUI users corrupt their mental model of the DB is not knowing they're inside a transaction — or worse, inside an *aborted* one where every statement returns 'current transaction is aborted'. qwry's one-connection-per-tab design makes this tractable and tokio-postgres exposes the ReadyForQuery transaction-status byte (idle/in-txn/failed-txn) after every statement. BEYOND: a status-bar chip that flips idle→IN TXN→TXN FAILED in real time, one-key COMMIT/ROLLBACK bound next to it, the close-guard extended to warn on open transactions (not just uncommitted cell edits), and when a statement fails mid-script the error banner says 'transaction aborted — ⌘⌫ to rollback'. FITS CHARTER: core correctness — 'never lies about data' includes never lying about transaction state. No competitor surfaces failed-txn state well.

findings.title: Unsafe-query guard: UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE (DataGrip unsafe query warning)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip warns before executing DELETE or UPDATE with no WHERE clause. WHY LOVED: it's the seatbelt everyone has needed exactly once; costs nothing until it saves a table. qwry has DangerModal + planned prod read-only mode, but nothing inspects the SQL itself. BEYOND: lint-level highlight (yellow gutter) the moment you type a WHERE-less UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, and an execute-time interstitial showing the parsed target table + 'affects ALL rows' with the row estimate from reltuples (already planned in v0.4 introspection) — 'this will update ~2.4M rows in orders'. On prod-flagged connections escalate to type-the-table-name confirm. Detection is a trivial walk of the existing lezer tree. FITS CHARTER: core safety for a user who points this at prod-shaped DBs.

findings.title: Go-to-table from anywhere + insert-at-caret (DataGrip double-Shift / ⌘O navigation)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip's Search Everywhere jumps to any table/view/procedure by fuzzy name from any context, and ⌘B on an identifier in SQL navigates to the object's definition. WHY LOVED: with 300 tables the tree is a scroll trap; typing 5 characters is faster than any click path. qwry's ⌘K palette exists and the SchemaSnapshot is in memory. BEYOND: index every table/view/column/function into the palette with fuzzy match + usage-frequency ranking (the completion engine already persists usage counts — reuse them); Enter opens a table tab, ⌘Enter inserts the qualified name at the editor caret, ⌥Enter reveals in sidebar tree; ⌘-click (or F12) on any identifier in the editor jumps to its structure view — resolved from the same context walker, zero IPC. FITS CHARTER: perfectly keyboard-first; latency budget trivially met from in-memory snapshot.

findings.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE upgrades: option toggles, actual-vs-estimate badges, hotspot heat (DataGrip diagram + pgAdmin graphical explain)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip renders plans as table or diagram (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+U); pgAdmin's graphical EXPLAIN adds per-node buffers/timing/WAL toggles and per-node stats tooltips with cost-based image shading. WHY LOVED: reading raw EXPLAIN text is a skill; a tree with the slow node glowing is instant diagnosis. qwry already has explain/ plan tree — ahead of TablePlus — so this is extend-the-lead territory. BEYOND: (a) one keystroke ⌘⇧E explains the statement under caret without editing SQL; (b) toolbar toggles for ANALYZE/BUFFERS/TIMING/SETTINGS/WAL that re-run and persist as prefs; (c) per-node badges where rows-estimated vs rows-actual diverge >10× (the #1 signal of stale stats / missing extended statistics); (d) nodes heat-colored by share of actual total time; (e) 'copy plan as text/JSON' for sharing. FITS CHARTER: yes — a tree view, keyboard-invoked, no dashboard sprawl.

findings.title: Per-table statistics in the Structure tab (pgAdmin Statistics tab PG-depth)
findings.detail: WHAT: pgAdmin shows per-table stats: live/dead tuples, last vacuum/autovacuum/analyze times, seq scans vs index scans, table+index+toast sizes; per-index scan counts reveal dead indexes. WHY LOVED: answers 'why is this table slow / is this index used / when did autovacuum last run' without memorizing pg_stat_user_tables columns — pure PG-depth that generic clients lack. qwry's v0.4 already plans reltuples + pg_total_relation_size; this is the natural superset. BEYOND: a Stats section in the existing structure tab, fetched lazily on expand with ONE query joining pg_stat_user_tables + pg_statio + pg_indexes sizes; render index rows with an idx_scan=0 'never used' dim badge and a dead-tuple ratio bar; ⌘C copies any stat. No polling, no graphs — a one-shot snapshot with a refresh key. FITS CHARTER: yes — PG-only depth as static data in an existing surface, zero ongoing cost.

findings.title: FK navigation both directions + navigation history (DataGrip FK links)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip renders FK values as navigable links to the referenced row, and offers reverse navigation ('Referencing rows' — which children point at this row). WHY LOVED: it turns the grid into a browsable object graph — the 'magic' moment in every DataGrip demo. qwry v0.45 already plans FK picker + jump-to-row; endorse and extend. BEYOND: (a) reverse-FK — on a PK cell, 'Show referencing rows ▸' lists each inbound FK (already in SchemaSnapshot both-directions) and opens the child table filtered to this key; (b) a per-tab navigation stack so ⌘[ / ⌘] walk back/forward across FK jumps like a browser — nobody has this and it's what makes graph-walking safe; (c) FK hover shows a mini-preview of the referenced row (single indexed lookup, cached). FITS CHARTER: core — direct manipulation + keyboard-first; the nav stack is the step beyond DataGrip.

findings.title: Query macros with $SELECTION$ placeholders bound to keys (pgAdmin Query Tool Macros)
findings.detail: WHAT: pgAdmin lets you bind predefined SQL to a keypress, with $SELECTION$ substituted by the current editor selection at run time. WHY LOVED: every DBA has 5 ritual queries (find blocking locks, table sizes, running queries, kill by pid) and re-typing or hunting saved files is friction; one-key ritual queries are addictive. qwry has SavedQueries but they're inert text. BEYOND: saved queries become palette verbs with a context-aware placeholder set richer than pgAdmin's — $SELECTION$ (editor selection), $TABLE$ (focused table tab / sidebar selection), $CELL$ (focused grid cell value, properly quoted by type), $DB$ — plus optional per-query keybinding. Ship 4-5 built-in 'PG toolbox' macros (blockers, sizes, activity, dead indexes) so the value is visible on day one. FITS CHARTER: perfectly — keyboard-first, turns persistence surface into a power feature.

findings.title: Raw-WHERE filter bar with full completion in the table browser (DataGrip data editor filter field)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip's data editor has a WHERE field under the toolbar — type a raw predicate, it re-SELECTs with it; also per-column filter pickers and filter-by-selected-value from the cell menu. WHY LOVED: structured filter UIs cap out fast; SQL users just want to type `status='paid' AND created_at > now()-interval '1 day'` with completion. qwry's browser has structured filters; the roadmap's cell menu adds filter-by-value. BEYOND: a ⌘L filter bar accepting a raw WHERE fragment powered by the SAME schema-aware completion engine scoped to the browsed table (no competitor gives filter-bar intellisense this good), per-table filter history (last 10, arrow-up to recall, persisted in appdb), and structured filters + raw fragment composing with AND. Column-header distinct-value picker (roadmap) stays for the mouse path. FITS CHARTER: core — SQL-first GUI-equal in one feature.

findings.title: Result-set diff, including cross-connection (DataGrip Compare Data with tolerance)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip diffs two grids (result vs result, table vs table) in a diff viewer with cell-level highlight and a numeric tolerance parameter. WHY LOVED: 'did staging and prod diverge' / 'what changed after my script ran' is otherwise manual eyeballing or hand-written EXCEPT queries. BEYOND: 'Compare with…' on a result tab picks another result tab; rows keyed by PK when the editability map knows it (falling back to row order), added/removed/changed rows tinted, changed cells show old→new. The killer variant qwry can own: run the SAME query against two connections (staging vs prod — this user's daily reality) and diff in one action. Client-side over the 50k cap with an honest capped indicator, same as find-in-results. FITS CHARTER: yes, as an on-demand view; medium effort, defer to post-v0.5 but design the result-tab model to allow it (see pinned results).

findings.title: Pinned result panes / multiple results per tab (DataGrip tabbed results)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip keeps each execution's result in its own tab under the console and lets you pin one so re-runs don't overwrite it. WHY LOVED: iterate-on-query workflows constantly need 'the result from before my change' next to 'after'. qwry replaces the per-tab result on every run — history preserves the SQL but not the rows. BEYOND: a lightweight 'pin this result' (📌 key on the results header) that freezes the current statement grid as a read-only pane; next run renders below/beside it; unpin discards. Cap at one pin per tab to protect memory (50k-row cap × 2). This is also the structural prerequisite for result-diff above. FITS CHARTER: yes with the memory cap stated honestly; avoids DataGrip's tab-sprawl by allowing exactly one pin.

findings.title: 'Who is blocking me' one-key lock diagnosis (pgAdmin locks view, weaponized)
findings.detail: WHAT: pgAdmin's dashboard shows pg_locks joined to sessions; DBAs use it to find lock chains. WHY LOVED: a hanging UPDATE with no feedback is the scariest moment in a DB client; pgAdmin at least lets you go look. qwry can do better than a passive view. BEYOND: when a statement in a qwry tab runs >Ns, the status bar offers 'Show blockers' — one keystroke runs pg_blocking_pids(active_pid) + pg_stat_activity on a side connection and renders the blocking chain (pid, user, app_name, query, age) as a plain grid with a 'cancel blocker' action (pg_cancel_backend, gated by DangerModal on prod). qwry knows its OWN backend pid per session, so this is precise, not a haystack. FITS CHARTER: yes — reactive and on-demand, not a polling dashboard; pairs with the v0.5 force-kill-session item. Post-v0.5 but cheap once session pids are tracked.

findings.title: Sessions/activity grid with cancel-terminate (pgAdmin server activity panel)
findings.detail: WHAT: pgAdmin's server activity tab lists pg_stat_activity sessions with state/wait-event/query and per-row cancel + terminate buttons; also locks and prepared-transactions tabs. WHY LOVED: 'what is hammering this database right now' is a weekly need; kill-runaway-query is the follow-up. qwry's roadmap defers the full activity monitor past v0.5 — right call. BEYOND (post-v0.5): skip the dedicated dashboard entirely; ship it as a built-in macro ('Server activity' palette verb) that opens a normal result grid of pg_stat_activity with row context-menu actions Cancel backend / Terminate backend (DangerModal + prod guard). The grid IS the activity monitor — no new surface, sortable/filterable/copyable for free, refresh on ⌘R. FITS CHARTER: the grid-native version fits; a live auto-refreshing dashboard does not (polling violates latency-first idle behavior).

findings.title: Paste external CSV/TSV into the grid as staged edits (DataGrip clipboard paste)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip parses clipboard TSV/CSV on paste into the data editor, filling a rectangle of cells or appending rows. WHY LOVED: the spreadsheet→DB path is constant in real work (paste 20 IDs from a Slack thread, paste a corrected column from Excel). qwry has copy in multiple formats planned but paste is single-cell. BEYOND: paste detects tab/comma structure, maps columns left-to-right from the anchor cell, coerces values per column type (type-aware, with per-cell error badges on unparseable values), and stages everything through the existing editsStore so ⌘S shows the full generated UPDATE/INSERT preview before anything touches the DB — the preview step is the trust win over DataGrip's immediate apply. Multi-row paste below the last row feeds the inline add-row draft band as multiple INSERT drafts. FITS CHARTER: yes — never-corrupt-data is preserved by the stage+preview model qwry already has.

findings.title: Syntax-aware expand selection (DataGrip ⌘W / Opt+Up)
findings.detail: WHAT: repeatedly pressing expand-selection grows the selection by AST node — identifier → expression → clause → statement — and in the grid: cell → column → row → all. WHY LOVED: muscle-memory feature from IntelliJ; selecting 'the whole subquery' with 3 keypresses beats mouse-precision every time. qwry has the lezer tree in the editor and a selection model in the grid. BEYOND: ⌥↑/⌥↓ expand/shrink in the editor walking lezer nodes (near-free); in the grid, the same chord does cell→column→row→statement-grid, matching DataGrip's grid semantics so one mental model covers both surfaces. FITS CHARTER: pure keyboard-first polish, trivial latency.

findings.title: Live templates + postfix completion (DataGrip ⌘J templates, `table.afrom`)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip ships snippet templates (sel→SELECT * FROM, ins→INSERT) with tab-stops, plus postfix completion — type `orders.afrom` and it rewrites to `SELECT * FROM orders`. WHY LOVED: SQL is boilerplate-heavy; templates collapse the 20 keystrokes of an INSERT skeleton to 3. qwry's completion engine is custom and schema-aware — better raw material than DataGrip's. BEYOND: a small built-in template set (sel/selw/ins/upd/cte/jsonb-path) surfaced through the SAME completion popup (no separate ⌘J list), with tab-stops via CodeMirror snippet fields, and schema-aware placeholders — expanding `ins` after typing a table name pre-fills the column list from the snapshot. Postfix `.afrom`/`.count`/`.where` on any known table name. Skip user-defined template management UI for now (roadmap defers snippet UI — agreed). FITS CHARTER: yes, keystroke economy is the charter.

findings.title: Rename refactoring for aliases/CTEs, with ALTER-RENAME generation for real objects (DataGrip Shift+F6)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip's rename works on query-local symbols (aliases, CTE names) rewriting all usages in-buffer, and on real DB objects where it generates and runs the ALTER … RENAME, updating usages in other object sources. WHY LOVED: renaming an alias used 14 times by hand invites the one you missed; object rename with usage awareness is DDL-with-a-safety-net. BEYOND for qwry: phase 1 (cheap, high-value) — F2/⇧F6 on an alias or CTE name does in-buffer rename of all resolved usages via the lezer context walker, live-previewed as you type; phase 2 (post-v0.5, needs get_ddl era) — F2 on a table/column generates the ALTER RENAME into the editor (never auto-runs), gated by DangerModal + prod read-only. FITS CHARTER: phase 1 is pure editor intelligence fitting the intellisense differentiator; phase 2 is honest generate-don't-execute.

findings.title: Quick table peek / evaluate expression (DataGrip Ctrl+Alt+F8)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip evaluates the object under the caret — hover-invoke on a table name pops the first rows without opening a tab; on an expression it shows the computed value. WHY LOVED: 'what does this table even look like' mid-query, answered without losing editor context or spawning tab clutter. BEYOND: ⌘E (peek) on a table identifier opens an anchored overlay (the v0.3 overlay primitive!) with a mini-grid of `SELECT * … LIMIT 20` + column count + row estimate from the snapshot; Esc dismisses, ⏎ promotes it to a real table tab. Same peek on a CTE name shows the CTE's SELECT run standalone — genuinely beyond DataGrip and trivially derivable from the parse tree. FITS CHARTER: yes — keyboard-first, uses existing overlay + streaming machinery with a tiny row cap.

findings.title: Statement outline + go-to-column popup (DataGrip ⌘F12 structure view / column list)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip's ⌘F12 in the editor pops a fuzzy-searchable outline of all statements in the script (jump to any); in the grid it pops a column list (jump to / show-hide columns by name). WHY LOVED: 500-line scratch files and 80-column tables are both navigation deserts; fuzzy-jump fixes both with one idiom. qwry's splitter already knows every statement range; the grid knows its columns. BEYOND: one ⌘F12 idiom, surface-scoped like ⌘F — in the editor it lists statements (first line + kind badge SELECT/UPDATE/DDL, Enter jumps, ⌘Enter runs); in the grid it lists columns with type icons, Enter scrolls-to-column, Space toggles visibility (wiring the v0.4 column-hide feature to keyboard). FITS CHARTER: exactly the find-system consistency philosophy already in the roadmap.

findings.title: History entries carry duration/rows/error + restore-with-diff (DataGrip query history + pgAdmin history panel)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip's history is searchable per-datasource; pgAdmin's history panel records status, duration, rows affected, and offses copy-back-to-editor with a source label. WHY LOVED: history is only useful if it answers 'which of my 30 attempts was the fast/correct one' — bare SQL text doesn't. qwry's v0.5 History panel + the failed-queries-recorded bug fix are already planned; this shapes them. BEYOND: record duration_ms, row_count, error text, and connection per entry (columns already flowing through QueryEvent::StatementDone); History panel groups identical SQL (run 12×, sparkline of durations — catches 'this got slow today'); Enter re-runs, ⌘Enter restores into the editor showing an inline diff against the current buffer when they differ. FITS CHARTER: yes — pure appdb + existing event data.

findings.title: Object source viewer + jump-to-source (DataGrip DDL view, endorses v0.4 get_ddl)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip shows any object's generated DDL/source and navigates from usage to definition; pgAdmin's SQL tab does the same per selected object. WHY LOVED: 'what does this view/function actually do' is answered in-place instead of via \d+ in psql. qwry's v0.4 get_ddl backend (pg_get_viewdef/functiondef/indexdef) is planned for Copy DDL. BEYOND copy: a read-only source *view* — Enter on a view/function in the sidebar (or F12 on its name in SQL) opens a syntax-highlighted read-only editor tab of its definition, with the same completion-hover affordances; from a function's completion popup entry, ⌥Enter jumps to its source. Read-only tabs marked with the existing read-only-says-why pattern. FITS CHARTER: yes — reuses editor + get_ddl; big step past Copy-DDL-to-clipboard.

findings.title: Maintenance actions with streamed VERBOSE output (pgAdmin Maintenance dialog)
findings.detail: WHAT: pgAdmin's per-table Maintenance dialog runs VACUUM/ANALYZE/REINDEX/CLUSTER with option checkboxes and shows server messages. WHY LOVED: these are the PG rituals everyone runs after bulk loads; a dialog beats remembering syntax. BEYOND: sidebar table context-menu 'Maintenance ▸ VACUUM / VACUUM FULL / ANALYZE / REINDEX' items that just generate the statement into a query tab (never auto-run — qwry's generate-don't-execute trust model), and — the real win — surface RAISE NOTICE / VERBOSE lines live in the results area via the QueryEvent::Notice channel that v0.5 already plans to stop dropping. Watching 'INFO: vacuuming public.orders' stream in is psql-parity no Mac GUI has. FITS CHARTER: yes — notices work is already roadmapped; menu items are one-liners on the v0.3 menu system.

findings.title: Per-connection init SQL / session-setup script (DataGrip data source startup script)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip lets each data source run a startup script and set a default schema/search_path per console. WHY LOVED: real environments need `SET search_path`, `SET work_mem`, role switches (`SET ROLE readonly`) on every session; without it users paste the same preamble forever. qwry's v0.5 connection-time session setup (statement_timeout, TimeZone, application_name) is planned as fixed fields. BEYOND: add one free-text 'Session init SQL' field per profile, executed after the built-in SETs on every new tab session, with failures surfaced via ConnToast (not silently swallowed); show an 'init' chip in the status bar when custom init ran so sessions are never mysteriously different. FITS CHARTER: yes — tiny driver addition, big daily-driver payoff, honest about session state.

findings.title: Connection color propagated as ambient safety chrome (DataGrip data source colors)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip assigns a color per data source that tints editor tabs, result toolbars, and dialogs — the visual 'you are on PROD' signal; pgAdmin lets you name/color server groups. WHY LOVED: environment mix-ups are the most expensive class of GUI accident; ambient color is the cheapest prevention. qwry has rail avatar colors + is_prod flag but the work surface itself is environment-blind. BEYOND: the profile color (and especially is_prod) tints a 2px border around the main card + the tab strip underline + the grid header accent; prod additionally gets a persistent 'PROD · read-only' chip in the breadcrumb that doubles as the toggle for the planned write-enable. Theme-engine-native (one more derived token), so it stays beautiful, not alarmish. FITS CHARTER: core safety multiplier for the v0.5 prod safe-mode; near-zero cost.

findings.title: Recent-locations switcher (DataGrip ⌘E recent files)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip's ⌘E pops recently-opened consoles/tables for instant switchback; IntelliJ users live in it. WHY LOVED: DB work is 3 tables + 2 queries revisited constantly; the tree and even the tab strip are slower than 'the last thing I touched'. qwry's Dashboard has recent activity but it's a home-screen affordance, not a mid-flow one. BEYOND: ⌘E overlay listing recent tabs + recently browsed tables + recent queries in one frecency-ranked list (appdb already logs the raw events), Enter switches/reopens, works identically from editor/grid/browser. Also fixes the roadmap-noted palette gap ('palette can't focus an existing tab') as a specialized, faster path. FITS CHARTER: keyboard-first tab economy; overlay primitive makes it cheap.

findings.title: Plan history + regression compare per query (beyond both tools)
findings.detail: WHAT (seed): DataGrip 2026.1 shipped 'explain plan flow enhancements' and both tools render single plans well — but neither remembers plans. WHY IT MATTERS: the actual workflow is 'add index → re-explain → did the plan change?' and today users eyeball two trees from memory. BEYOND (qwry-original, enabled by local-first): persist the last N plans per normalized-query-hash in appdb; the explain view gets a history strip — select two runs to see a structural diff (node added/removed, cost/time deltas colored), with a badge on re-explain when the plan shape changed since last run ('plan changed: Seq Scan → Index Scan'). Local-only storage honors the no-telemetry charter. FITS CHARTER: yes — a genuine surpass-not-catch-up feature sitting on the existing explain visualizer + appdb.

findings.title: pg_settings viewer as a plain grid (pgAdmin server configuration tab)
findings.detail: WHAT: pgAdmin's dashboard includes a server-config table of pg_settings; DBAs use it to check work_mem/shared_buffers/track_io_timing without SHOW-ing one by one. WHY LOVED: config archaeology is common when diagnosing slowness. BEYOND: no new surface — a palette verb 'Server settings' opens a result grid of `SELECT name, setting, unit, source, short_desc FROM pg_settings` with a preset quick-filter for source ≠ 'default' (the only rows anyone cares about); pairs with the v0.5 server-info card (version/encoding/search_path). FITS CHARTER: fits precisely BECAUSE it's just a grid + macro — build it as a built-in macro, not a feature.

findings.title: Lightweight parameterized queries (DataGrip user parameters)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip detects :name/$1/? placeholders (with user-configurable regex patterns per dialect), prompts for values, and remembers them per query. WHY LOVED: lets you keep one canonical query and re-run with different IDs; essential for queries pasted from application logs. CHARTER TENSION: qwry's roadmap explicitly defers this below the 'minimum real DB client' line — defensible for v0.5. BEYOND (post-v0.5, keep it small): detect $1/:param on run, render an inline value bar above the results (not a modal — modals break flow), coerce by inferred type, persist last values per query hash in appdb, and send via the extended protocol (tokio-postgres params) so quoting is impossible to get wrong — a correctness win over DataGrip's textual substitution. Mark: fits charter later, correctly sequenced after v0.5.

findings.title: ERD tool — DOESN'T FIT; steal the intent as a text-first FK map (pgAdmin ERD tool)
findings.detail: WHAT: pgAdmin generates entity-relationship diagrams per schema/table (tables plotted with FK links, DDL generation from diagram). WHY LOVED: newcomers to a schema orient via relationships. CHARTER VERDICT: correctly deferred by the roadmap — canvas diagrams are mouse-first, layout-heavy, and violate the latency ethos on big schemas. STEAL THE INTENT: a 'Relations' section in the table structure tab listing outbound FKs (col → target.col) and inbound FKs (source.col → col) as navigable rows (Enter browses the related table pre-filtered) — the SchemaSnapshot already holds FKs both directions, so this is a render-only feature that answers 90% of what people open ERDs for.

findings.title: Schema diff — DOESN'T FIT v0.5; note the cheap local variant (pgAdmin Schema Diff)
findings.detail: WHAT: pgAdmin's Schema Diff compares two databases/schemas object-by-object and generates the sync DDL script into a query tab. WHY LOVED: 'did the migration land the same on staging and prod' is otherwise pure pain. CHARTER VERDICT: roadmap defers migration-gen — right for v0.5; full sync-script generation is a product in itself. CHEAP LOCAL VARIANT worth remembering: qwry already captures full SchemaSnapshots per connection — a client-side structural diff of two snapshots (tables/columns/types/indexes present here, missing there) rendered as a tree with added/removed/changed tints is introspection-reuse, ~zero backend work, and explicitly NOT a DDL generator. Post-v0.5, staging-vs-prod is this user's literal weekly workflow.

findings.title: Live dashboard graphs (TPS/sessions/block-IO) — DOESN'T FIT (pgAdmin monitoring graphs)
findings.detail: WHAT: pgAdmin's dashboard polls and charts transactions/sec, session counts, block I/O per server/database. WHY LOVED: ops people like ambient graphs. CHARTER VERDICT: does not fit — continuous polling contradicts qwry's local-fast idle discipline, charts aren't keyboard-first, and real monitoring belongs in Grafana. The on-demand substitutes above (activity macro, blockers, per-table stats) capture the diagnostic value without the dashboard. Also skip pgAdmin's prepared-transactions tab (niche 2PC) and the embedded PSQL terminal (duplicates the editor; qwry's editor + notices + transaction chip should reach psql-parity instead).

findings.title: Create table from result / export-to-database (DataGrip Export to Database)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip can materialize any result set (or CSV) into a new table in a chosen schema, with column mapping. WHY LOVED: 'snapshot this query result so I can join against it tomorrow' is a real analyst move. BEYOND (small, honest version): a result-grid action 'Copy as CREATE TABLE AS' that generates `CREATE TABLE _scratch AS <the tab's SQL>` into the editor (generate-don't-execute), and 'Copy as CREATE TABLE (DDL)' inferring column types from the result's type_oids — clipboard-only, no wizard. The full import/mapping wizard stays deferred per the roadmap. FITS CHARTER: the clipboard variant does; the wizard doesn't (yet).

findings.title: SQL log — every statement the app ran, greppable (DataGrip SQL log)
findings.detail: WHAT: DataGrip writes literally every query the IDE issues (including its own introspection) to a text log reachable from the Help menu. WHY LOVED: trust and debuggability — when the tool misbehaves or you need 'what exactly did I run at 15:42 yesterday', the log settles it; it's also how users discover what a GUI does behind their back. BEYOND: qwry already distinguishes user SQL (history) from machinery; add an opt-in session log file in app-data that records user statements AND app-issued introspection/edit statements with timestamps + connection — radical transparency that reinforces the no-telemetry, never-lies brand ('here is every byte we sent your server'). Rotating, capped, off by default. FITS CHARTER: philosophically on-brand; low urgency.
